"What we’ve used is peanuts," Trump said. "We have a lot of mid-level weapons."

Eric Mack is a breaking news reporter and writer Sunday through Thursday, 6 a.m. ET to 2 p.m. ET, with a particular interest in stories that lead the news cycle on politics, elections, foreign affairs and government.

title: Australia sets launch for sweeping gun buyback after Bondi Beach terror attack: 'Sensible gun reform'
summary: New South Wales will be the first Australian state to launch a gun buyback scheme, offering up to $700 per firearm after the Bondi Beach terror attack.
story: Fox News correspondent Steve Harrigan reports from Bondi Beach after new police documents detail the Sydney Hanukkah terror attack, including pipe bombs and an ISIS flag, as anger grows over Australia’s response to rising antisemitism.

New South Wales in Australia is slated to begin a gun buyback scheme in November, the first state in the nation to kick off the program as part of the national response to a shooting spree that killed 15 people at a Hanukkah celebration in the state capital of Sydney, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced on Sunday.

Albanese and New South Wales Premier Chris Minns said the scheme would start on November 2. People who return eligible firearms under the first phase would receive fixed compensation ranging from $450 to $1,000 per firearm, depending on the type. A second phase will provide a valuation pathway for certain higher-value firearms, capped at $10,000 per firearm.

Albanese's center-left government adopted new gun-control laws in January in the aftermath of the December 14 attack at a Bondi Beach Hanukkah celebration, including the gun buyback program and tighter firearms measures. New South Wales separately passed tighter state firearms laws in December, while the federal government also strengthened laws targeting hate speech and extremism.

The pair of alleged gunmen used firearms that were obtained legally. Australia's government said there were a record 4.1 million firearms in the country last year, including more than 1.1 million in New South Wales, its most populous state.
AUSTRALIA VOWS TO STRENGTHEN HATE SPEECH LAWS, GUN CONTROL IN WAKE OF BONDI BEACH ATTACK

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's government adopted new gun-control laws in January in the aftermath of the December 14 attack at a Bondi Beach Hanukkah celebration. (Hollie Adams/Reuters)
"We must do everything we can to make sure the antisemitic terrorist attack in Bondi doesn’t happen again. That includes meaningful nationwide gun reform," Albanese said in a statement.
The initiative is set to be Australia's largest buyback since a similar effort following the 1996 massacre in Tasmania's Port Arthur, when a gunman killed 35 people.
"Australians are quite rightly proud of our gun laws, but the fact is there are more guns in Australia today than there were at the time of dealing with the Port Arthur gun buyback," Albanese said.

New South Wales generally limits individual firearm ownership to four guns under restrictions sparked by the Bondi Beach attack, with exemptions allowing certain license holders, including some primary producers, sport shooters and others with specified genuine reasons, to possess more firearms. It estimates that up to 274,000 registered firearms — about 24% of the total number of registered firearms in New South Wales — and about 50,000 license holders are affected by the new limits on gun ownership and reclassification of some types of firearms.
VIRGINIA GUN SALES SPIKE AHEAD OF JULY 1 ASSAULT WEAPONS BAN SIGNED BY GOV. SPANBERGER
Australia's government said there were a record 4.1 million firearms in the country last year, including more than 1.1 million in New South Wales. (Steve Markham/AP Photo)

"After Bondi, we promised the people of New South Wales we would introduce the toughest gun laws in the country, and that’s exactly what we did," Minns said. "The next step is getting the guns that are no longer permitted under those laws out of circulation and permanently off our streets."

"There are potentially hundreds of thousands of firearms affected by these changes," Minns added. "We want those guns handed in, compensated for and safely destroyed. This is a big undertaking, but the principle behind it is simple: fewer dangerous guns in our community means a safer New South Wales."
The attack was allegedly carried out by a father and son who police believe were inspired by the Islamic State.

The 50-year-old father, Sajid Akram, was shot and killed by police at the scene, while the surviving suspect, Naveed Akram, 24, has not yet entered pleas on a slew of charges, including 15 counts of murder. Authorities have charged him with 59 offenses in total, including committing a terrorist act and 15 counts of murder.
The attack was carried out by a father and son who police believe were inspired by the Islamic State. (Steve Markham/AP Photo)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
A man identified as Ahmed al Ahmed has been praised as a hero for tackling and disarming one of the gunmen. He suffered gunshot wounds in the incident and is still recovering.

"After the tragedy at Bondi, we committed to dealing with the motive and the method," Minister for Home Affairs Tony Burke said. "Since then, we have strengthened our hate crimes and hate speech laws, which are now the strongest in our country’s history."
"Today we continue the proud Australian tradition of sensible gun reform designed to protect our community from weapons which have no utility other than to cause harm," he added.

title: Iran war thrusts Diego Garcia into spotlight as official calls US military base ‘integral’
summary: Diego Garcia supports U.S. carrier strike groups and supply chains after an Iranian strike on Bahrain forced the Pentagon to shift logistics.
story: President Trump threatens to deploy ICE agents to US airports, sparking debate over DHS funding and airport security. This comes as Iran targets a joint US-UK military base in the Indian Ocean with intermediate-range ballistic missiles, demonstrating a significant military capability. Experts discuss the Natanz nuclear facility, missile production, and the need for NATO allies to engage in securing the Strait of Hormuz.

An official with the self-described Chagossian government-in-exile said Sunday that the war with Iran has underscored Diego Garcia’s strategic importance to U.S. forces and Middle East regional stability, with the Pentagon shifting logistics to the remote U.K.-U.S. base in the Indian Ocean after an Iranian strike on a major American installation in Bahrain.

The base, in the southern Chagos Archipelago, has reportedly supported carrier strike groups including the USS Abraham Lincoln, whose forces have conducted air operations and helped enforce the blockade of Iranian ports.

The U.S. military’s wartime logistics network now stretches across a roughly 2,200-mile maritime supply route to Diego Garcia, allowing forces to avoid coastal facilities vulnerable to Iranian attacks but requiring longer shuttle runs and slower replenishment, according to The New York Times.

"That is an inconvenience, but it shows the importance of the base," James Tumbridge, an international lawyer who serves as attorney general for the Chagossian government-in-exile, told Fox News Digital.
UK DEFENSE SHORTFALLS HIGHLIGHTED AS BRITAIN AVOIDS IRAN OFFENSIVE ROLE AMID TRUMP CRITICISM
Diego Garcia is a strategic Indian Ocean base hosting 2,500 US military personnel. (Reuters)
"The base is integral to regional security for the U.K., U.S. and our allies. This latest news emphasizes it."
"Bahrain is a far easier target, so the U.S. change of supply arrangement makes sense," Tumbridge said, adding, "Hopefully the new British PM will not deny the U.S. this change of use."

"It shows the importance of the base and asking a third country for permission is not what the U.S. will want, and so I hope this means Trump will still oppose the handover," Tumbridge went on to say, referring to a proposed agreement that would transfer sovereignty of the Chagos Islands to Mauritius.

In 2025, the U.K. and Mauritius signed a treaty that would recognize Mauritian sovereignty over the Chagos Archipelago while allowing the U.K. to retain control of Diego Garcia for an initial 99-year period.
The British government later put implementation of the agreement on hold amid renewed U.S. concerns over the sovereignty transfer.
STARMER IN 'SEISMIC' CRISIS, UK DEFENSE CHIEF QUITS BEFORE HIGH-STAKES TRUMP NATO SUMMIT
Keir Starmer, leader of Britain's Labour Party, speaks during the Prime Minister's Questions, at the House of Commons in London, Britain November 15, 2023. (UK Parliament/Maria Unger/Handout)

Reports emerged in June that U.S. officials had drafted a proposal to bypass Britain and strike a deal to take control of Diego Garcia, one of several alternatives to then-Prime Minister Keir Starmer's plan to transfer sovereignty to Mauritius.

The first minister of the self-described Chagossian government-in-exile responded that month and said the Chagos Islands were not for sale or "for stealing either," but argued that he "can’t blame" Trump for "looking to secure the military base."
"Trump cannot buy the islands. That suggestion made by some is unhelpful to us all. Only the U.K. can sell the islands, as only the U.K. owns them," Tumbridge also said on Sunday.
"The arguments over sovereignty do not get fixed via a sale, and Mauritius cannot sell them unless the U.K. first gives them away," he added.
"It is not in the U.K.’s interest to sell them. Whether we keep them and continue our support for the U.S. base or we cede them to Mauritius is the choice — my desire is the former."
Mauritius has long claimed sovereignty over the archipelago, a position backed by a 2019 advisory opinion from the International Court of Justice and subsequent U.N. action.

The U.K. government, however, permitted the U.S. to use Diego Garcia for limited defensive operations targeting Iranian missile capabilities in March after initially withholding approval for offensive strikes.
GULF COUNTRIES STRONGLY CONDEMN IRAN'S DRONE ATTACK ON BAHRAIN AS RISING TENSIONS THREATEN MOU

A U.S. B-2 Spirit bomber, part of the 509th Bomb Wing at Whiteman Air Force Base in Missouri, stops for refueling at the U.S. military base on Diego Garcia in October 2001, following an airstrike mission over Afghanistan in support of Operation Enduring Freedom. (U.S. Department of Defense/Senior Airman Rebeca M. Luquin)

"The U.S. wanted to use Chagos Diego Garcia for air strikes at the very beginning. The U.K. consulted Mauritius and refused — hence Trump finally appreciating why sovereignty transfer was a problem," Tumbridge said.
"After the attacks on Cyprus, the U.K. allowed certain so-called defense uses, and Iran did fire at Diego Garcia, but they missed."
On March 20, Reuters reported that Iran had fired two ballistic missiles toward Diego Garcia.

One missile failed in flight, while a U.S. warship fired an interceptor at the other, though it was initially unclear whether the interception succeeded. British officials later said one missile fell short and the other was intercepted.
"No serious concerns have been shared — the earlier attempt showed a lack of range and targeting ability," Tumbridge said.

"The British Government and the Commissioner for the Territory have already tried to say the last attack makes the islands unsafe. No one seriously believes that Iran would try to target the outer islands that presently only have a population of six people."
PENTAGON RACES TO BUY 10X MORE MISSILES AS IRAN WAR DWINDLES ARSENAL, THREATENS READINESS FOR CHINA AGGRESSION
Diego Garcia, the largest island in the Chagos archipelago and site of a major United States military base in the middle of the Indian Ocean, leased from the UK in 1966. (Reuters)
The reported U.S. logistical strains and renewed focus on Diego Garcia came as the USS Abraham Lincoln approached nine months of continuous deployment in the region.
Speaking at Joint Base Andrews on Aug. 14, Trump said a new aircraft carrier was heading to the Middle East to replace it.
"That ship is moving," Trump said when reporters asked about the carrier.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Meanwhile, Adm. Brad Cooper, commander of U.S. Central Command, also met with service members aboard the carrier, which is expected to be relieved amid concerns raised by families over the extended deployment.
Fox News Digital has reached out to the Pentagon for comment.

Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.

title: Bab el-Mandeb Strait faces growing threat as Houthi attacks raise fears of a second Hormuz
summary: Iran-backed Houthis exploit Yemen's fractured state to threaten Bab el-Mandeb, raising fears it could become a second Strait of Hormuz choke point.
story: Tawakkol Karman tells Fox News Digital that restoring the Yemeni state is the only path to lasting peace and countering the Iran-backed Houthis.
The Iran-backed Houthis’ escalating attacks on shipping through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait are raising a growing strategic question: Could the waterway become the next Strait of Hormuz?

The answer is complicated by the geography — and by Yemen itself. Unlike Hormuz, where Iran can directly threaten shipping from its own coastline, Tehran’s leverage over Bab el-Mandeb depends largely on its Houthi allies. And the country overlooking the strait is fractured among competing armed and political forces, leaving the U.S. and its regional allies confronting a threat that may be difficult to solve with naval power alone.

The danger was underscored Tuesday when the Houthis attacked the Egyptian-owned cargo ship Tihamah in Bab el-Mandeb. Four crew members — three Pakistanis and one Indonesian — were killed, according to Yemeni and Pakistani officials, while two Yemeni rescuers were killed when the Houthis struck again after rescue crews arrived, Yemen’s Coast Guard said. Reuters reported that the fatalities, if confirmed, would be the first deaths in a Houthi strike on shipping since the U.S.-Iran war began Feb. 28.
IRAN-BACKED HOUTHI THREAT IN RED SEA COULD LEAD TO MAJOR US POLICY SHIFT, ANALYSTS SAY
Yemeni soldiers patrol the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait, Yemen, April 5, 2026. (Abdulnasser Alseddik/AP Photo)

The Bab el-Mandeb Strait, is located between Yemen and the Horn of Africa, connects the Gulf of Aden and Arabian Sea to the Red Sea and, farther north, the Suez Canal and the Mediterranean. It is a crucial route for energy and commercial shipping. The Suez Canal and Egypt’s SUMED pipeline effectively form the northern end of the same Red Sea corridor.
But the southern side of that corridor borders a country that has been at war for more than a decade.

The Houthis control the capital, Sanaa, and much of northern Yemen, while the internationally recognized, Saudi-backed government and an array of allied or competing groups control areas elsewhere. The Southern Transitional Council, a separatist movement that has been backed by the United Arab Emirates, has been a major force in the south.
That fragmentation is becoming increasingly relevant to the security of the waterway.
IRAN-BACKED TERROR PROXY HOUTHIS THREATEN FRESH ATTACKS AFTER YEMEN AIRPORT STRIKE

Amr Al Bidh, the STC’s foreign affairs chief, told Fox News Digital that naval forces can defend individual vessels but cannot by themselves remove the threat posed by Houthi-controlled territory overlooking the maritime route.
"Naval presence protects individual ships. It does not take away Houthi launch sites, it does not interdict the smuggling routes that resupply them and it does not hold terrain," Al Bidh said.
He said that "you have to be on the ground" to ultimately secure Bab el-Mandeb.
Vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, as seen from Musandam, Oman, on Aug. 3, 2026. (Reuters)

The deterioration comes amid a broader escalation in Yemen. U.N. Special Envoy Hans Grundberg told the Security Council Thursday that the country faces its most serious threat of a return to large-scale war since the U.N.-brokered 2022 truce, warning that renewed Houthi attacks on commercial vessels risk drawing Yemen deeper into the wider regional confrontation.

That truce sharply reduced major fighting after years of war following the Houthis’ seizure of Sanaa in 2014 and the Saudi-led military intervention the following year. Though the formal truce expired in October 2022, large-scale hostilities remained comparatively limited for years.
IRAN BLOCKADE ‘GOING GLOBAL’ IS A WARNING SIGNAL TO CHINA AND RUSSIA

Yemen's Iran-backed armed Houthi group has warned they will move to shutter the Bab Al-Mandeb Strait through missile-drone attacks if Gulf nations join the US-Israel war on Iran. (Mohammed Hamoud/Getty Images)

On July 20, the Houthis declared what they called a naval blockade of Saudi Arabia, threatening vessels doing business with Saudi ports. Riyadh denies the Houthi accusation that Saudi Arabia has imposed a siege on Yemen.

A White House official, speaking on background, said the United States expects the Houthis to continue to uphold the terms of the ceasefire. The official said the Houthis "saw during Operation Rough Rider that the United States and President Trump will take necessary action to protect freedom of navigation and U.S. commercial shipping from Houthi terrorist attacks."

The official added that the United States is focused on protecting core national security interests — including freedom of navigation in the Red Sea — while "empowering our regional partners to take the lead in managing and resolving regional security challenges." The official said Washington is in continuous dialogue with Saudi Arabia and the Republic of Yemen government regarding regional stability.

United Against Nuclear Iran, citing Joint Maritime Information Center data, has put the decline in tanker transits since the July 20 blockade declaration at roughly 40%. UANI also said tankers have been observed broadcasting messages including "CHINESE OWNER" and "ARMED GUARD ON BOARD" through their tracking systems, apparently in an effort to reduce the chance of being targeted.
TRADE VESSEL STRUCK BY PROJECTILE IN STRAIT OF HORMUZ AMID US-IRAN TALKS

Thousands of people gather at Sabeen Square, under the control of the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen, to protest the killing of Iran’s supreme leader in U.S. and Israeli airstrikes on Iran, in Sanaa, Yemen on March 6, 2026. (Mohammed Hamoud/Anadolu via Getty Images)

China, meanwhile, has been in contact with the Houthis over safe passage for Chinese vessels, according to a July 28 Reuters report citing Chinese and regional sources. Four China-bound tankers had crossed Bab el-Mandeb following the blockade announcement as Beijing sought assurances for its shipping.
The economic stakes are rising because of what is happening hundreds of miles to the east.
Saudi Arabia has increasingly relied on its Red Sea export infrastructure as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has been disrupted by the U.S.-Iran conflict.
That makes the Red Sea both an alternative to Hormuz — and a potential second pressure point.
Yemeni Nobel Peace Prize laureate Tawakkol Karman warned at the United Nations Thursday that Yemen’s internal collapse is increasingly threatening interests far beyond its borders.

"This is no longer a Yemeni crisis alone," Karman said. "The continued collapse of the state in Yemen threatens international navigation and trade, energy security, and global supply chains and undermines regional and international peace and security."

Karman had been invited by Denmark, which holds the Security Council presidency, to brief council members, but Denmark’s deputy U.N. ambassador said "strong opposition" prevented the briefing from taking place. Karman instead addressed reporters outside the chamber.
In a separate interview with Fox News Digital, Karman argued that restoring a functioning Yemeni state is ultimately essential to defeating armed groups and securing the country.
TRUMP WARNS IRAN FIGHTING ISN'T OVER AS HE VOWS US WILL 'WIN' AS TALKS FADE

Houthi terrorists walk over British and U.S. flags at a rally in support of Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, and Houthi strikes on shipping in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden on Feb. 4, 2024, on the outskirts of Sana'a, Yemen. (Mohammed Hamoud/Getty Images)
"Yemeni people can do that," Karman said of defeating the Houthis and other militias. "We can be partners on saving the global and regional security."
"Without restoring Yemen, that means there is not any sustainable peace," she added.
But U.S. experts caution against treating Bab el-Mandeb as simply a second Hormuz.

"Iran doesn’t have the same direct influence on flows through the Bab al-Mandeb as it does for the Strait of Hormuz," Richard Goldberg, a senior advisor at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies and former National Security Council official, told Fox News Digital.
"The strategy would depend much more on proxies — Iraqi groups focusing fire on infrastructure and the Houthis focusing on the Red Sea," Goldberg said.

But he said there are limits to that strategy. "The Houthis act much more independently than they used to, and have not yet shown an interest to going to war against the world — just against Riyadh," Goldberg said.
He also pointed to one critical difference between the two waterways: ships that cannot safely cross Bab el-Mandeb can bypass the Red Sea entirely by sailing around Africa.
"Unlike Hormuz, shippers can go around the Red Sea if they really need to," Goldberg said. "It adds cost and time but it’s not a single point of failure like Hormuz."
The question facing U.S., Saudi Arabia and its partners is therefore how to prevent the Houthi threat from becoming more serious.

Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, left, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, center, and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif sign a defense agreement in Mecca, Saudi Arabia, on Aug. 7, 2026. (TUR Presidency/Murat Cetinmuhurdar/Handout/Anadolu via Getty Images)
Riyadh is now trying to assemble two overlapping layers of regional security cooperation.

Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement on Aug. 7, a mutual-defense pact that calls for high-level political and military coordination, joint exercises and deeper defense-industry cooperation. Turkey has stressed that the agreement is defensive and does not identify Iran or any other country as an enemy.

Dr. Aziz Alghashian, a Saudi foreign-policy researcher and senior non-resident fellow at Gulf International Forum, told Fox News Digital earlier this week that one immediate implication could be greater coordination against Iran-backed groups, particularly the Houthis.

Alghashian said the pact could produce a greater trilateral presence near the Saudi-Yemeni border, "especially in the maritime dimension," while allowing Riyadh to take a firmer collective approach toward Iran-backed militias even as it maintains a more diplomatic approach toward Tehran itself.
Separately, Saudi Arabia is leading an effort specifically focused on the waterways.

The Saudi Defense Ministry announced July 30 plans for a multinational maritime-defense coalition intended to protect freedom of navigation and commercial and energy routes through Bab el-Mandeb, the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden. Fourteen countries, including Turkey, Pakistan, Egypt, Sudan and Djibouti, initially backed the initiative.
Turkey’s Defense Ministry confirmed Thursday that Ankara is participating in meetings in Jeddah aimed at establishing the coalition.
Ships are anchored in the Strait of Hormuz on Aug. 10, 2026, off the coast of Bandar Abbas, Iran. (Ali Saeedi/Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

A State Department spokesperson separately told Fox News Digital that protecting commercial shipping through both the Red Sea and the Strait of Hormuz remains a "top priority" for the Trump administration, pointing to freedom of navigation as one of Washington’s core national security interests in the Middle East. "We will continue to work with international partners to deter Iranian and Iranian-proxy attacks on merchant vessels, ensure the free flow of commerce and hold accountable those who threaten the safety of international shipping lanes," a State Department spokesperson said.

The spokesperson said the administration is also seeking to disrupt the flow of Iranian money and weapons to the Houthis, noting that the U.S. has sanctioned more than 200 entities associated with the group.

"We condemn Iran’s flagrant violation of Yemen’s sovereignty and international law in threatening freedom of navigation and supporting their Houthi proxies," the spokesperson said. The State Department also emphasized Washington’s support for Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s internationally recognized government as the threat around Bab el-Mandeb grows.

"The United States stands firmly with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the internationally recognized government of Yemen against Houthi terrorism," the spokesperson said. "We are in close consultation with our Saudi and Yemeni partners and remain committed to their security."

Efrat (Effie) Lachter is a reporter for Fox News Digital with more than 15 years of experience covering conflict, global affairs, human rights and political accountability. She has directed and produced more than 200 documentary segments across more than 40 countries, documenting conflicts, humanitarian crises, corruption, human trafficking, gender-based violence and the human stories behind major world events.

Lachter’s reporting has taken her into conflict zones and crisis areas across the Middle East, Europe, Asia and Africa. Her work has included uncovering human trafficking networks, revealing an ISIS underground torture prison in Syria, documenting the war in Ukraine and interviewing senior political figures and world leaders. She was also among the Western journalists who entered Russia after the war began to bring testimonies from Putin’s opposition. Lachter is the recipient of the 2022 Peres Center for Peace Award and was a 2023–2024 Knight-Wallace Journalism Fellow at the University of Michigan. She also won two Rockower Awards for Excellence in Reporting. She holds a bachelor's degree in communication and a master's degree in political science.

title: Buffalo Bills’ Ed Oliver’s son has died, team announces
summary: The Buffalo Bills are mourning the death of defensive tackle Ed Oliver’s 2-year-old son, the team announced Saturday.
story: The Buffalo Bills are mourning the death of defensive tackle Ed Oliver’s 2-year-old son, the team announced Saturday.

“On behalf of the entire Buffalo Bills organization, we want to publicly express our condolences to Ed Oliver and his family on the devastating loss of his son. It’s an unthinkable tragedy for any parent. We will continue to support Ed and his family as we all grieve this tragic loss,” team general manager Brandon Beane said in a statement Saturday.
The team did not disclose the cause of death.

In June, however, authorities in Harris County, Texas,  responded to a report of a toddler drowning at an address that, according to property records, match the area where Oliver has a listed address.
Deputies responded to a report of a toddler found unresponsive in a swimming pool in the 500 block of Lago Trace Drive, the Harris County Sheriff’s Office said at the time.
“The toddler was transported to a local hospital, where they were pronounced deceased,” Sheriff Ed Gonzalez said at the time, without identifying the victim.
NBC News has reached out to the Harris County Sheriff’s Office and Oliver’s representatives for comment.
Oliver, 28, is from Houston, played college football for the Houston Cougars, and is entering his eighth NFL season with the Bills.

title: GOP lawmakers criticize Trump’s beef import plan amid blowback from ranchers
summary: House and Senate Republicans criticized President Donald Trump’s decision to suspend tariffs on ground beef imports, with lawmakers from agricultural states decrying the impact Trump’s decision will have on farmers.
story: House and Senate Republicans on Friday criticized President Donald Trump’s decision to suspend tariffs on ground beef imports, with lawmakers from agricultural states decrying the impact Trump’s decision will have on farmers.
Nebraska’s GOP senators, Deb Fischer and Pete Ricketts, said in separate posts on X that Trump’s decision was unwise.

“I’m extremely disappointed by this decision from the White House,” Fischer wrote. “We all want lower grocery prices, but as I’ve said for months, we cannot do it at the expense of American producers. Flooding the market with foreign beef hurts our livestock industry.”

Ricketts wrote: “I appreciate the Administration’s work to lower grocery prices. Short term policy shifts do not equal long term solutions. Flooding the market with lower quality beef compromises Nebraska farmers and ranchers.”

The president announced Friday on Truth Social that “the United States will allow up to 300,000 metric tons of product for ground beef to be imported with no out of quota tariff. We have a commitment that this beef will be sold at 25 percent below current market prices.”
Trump did not say which companies that import beef had agreed to this commitment or what countries would supply the meat.
Explaining his decision, the president pledged that this deal “will reduce prices for Americans while giving space for our Great American Beef Herd to grow again.”
Sen. Tim Sheehy, R-Mont., also cited the hardships American cattle farmers would face as a result of the president’s decision and referred to conversations he’s had with Trump about this issue.

“The President’s heart is in the right place on wanting lower prices for the American people, and beef prices have been impacted by the Mexican screwworm,” Sheehy wrote on X. “But the reality is this action will make it more difficult for American ranchers to rebuild our herd and bring prices down for the American people. And most importantly, this will harm our ranching families who feed the nation.”

Rep. Ashley Hinson, R-Iowa, who is running for Senate and received Trump’s endorsement in the race, also panned his announcement, writing in a post on X, “I want to lower prices but this is a bad idea.”

Hinson said that instead of allowing beef imports without tariffs, “We should be focused on cutting red tape for cattle producers, lowering the cost of production, and supporting market-based solutions to support Iowa producers and lower costs for consumers.”
Sen. Chuck Grassley, R-Iowa, writing in his custom shorthand on X, also expressed concern about Trump’s announcement, writing that “USA cattlemen shld always be put 1st thru America 1st policies.”
Grassley also expressed a “need 2keep up progress fighting screwworm+ expanding domestic herd.”
On Friday, the president defended his decision when asked at Joint Base Andrews about the criticism he was facing from fellow Republicans.

“Well, we want to get the beef prices down, so we’ll get them down a little bit, and that’s what people want. That’s what the voters want, and that’s what I want,” he told reporters. “The ranchers are great. They’re my people. I love the ranchers. They’ve done a fantastic job, but they admit that we need a little help, and in order to get the prices down, so that’s what we’re doing.”
The White House did not immediately respond to NBC News’ request for comment on the lawmakers’ criticisms of Trump’s plan.

U.S. cattle ranchers have faced headwinds for years that have sent beef prices higher, including shrinking supply. According to the American Farm Bureau Federation, the United States’ current cattle herd is the nation’s smallest since 1951.
A flesh-eating screwworm that targets cattle was also detected in the U.S. earlier this year for the first time in decades, further threatening cattle herds.
Trump first floated the idea of lowering imports on beef last year, but the notion was quickly shot down by a similar group of GOP senators from agricultural states.
“I represent a beef-producing state. We have four times as many cattle as people,” Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., said at the time, explaining his opposition.
On Friday, leaders for a top industry group representing cattle farmers, the National Cattlemen’s Beef Association, also said they were “disappointed” with Trump’s announcement.

“NCBA is disappointed by the President’s statement,” said Colin Woodall, the group’s chief executive officer. “While America’s cattle producers share the goal of keeping groceries affordable for consumers, flooding the market with government-subsidized, below-market beef is not the way to rebuild the American cattle herd.”
“Today’s announcement and other market interventions throw cold water on the prospect of herd expansion and sacrifices long-term stability for short term messaging,” Woodall added.

title: This is what you need (and need to do) to stay safe this hurricane season
summary: I talked to a meteorologist to find the best way to prepare for hurricanes and what products you should have on hand.
story: As a Florida native, I’ve endured a lot of hurricanes and I’ve seen the damage they can cause. If you don’t take proper precautions, the destruction hurricanes leave behind can be catastrophic. This is why it’s important to know how to prepare for a hurricane, and make sure you have all of the supplies necessary to keep you and your family safe. Storms have already started making their way across the United States, with tropical storm Lala impacting Hawaii earlier this week. Plus, a potentially record-breaking El Niño is growing in the Pacific ocean, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).

Power outages, flooding, broken windows and damage to homes and cars from fallen trees are just some of the things you need to be ready for. And while you may have a generator in case the electricity goes out, it’s important that you know how to use it properly to avoid carbon monoxide exposure.

I talked to a meteorologist and professor at the University of Florida to learn what measures you should take to make sure your home withstands a storm, and the best emergency kits and other supplies you should always have handy during hurricane season.

How to prepare for a hurricane
There are many different ways to prepare your home ahead of a hurricane to prevent damage, and to keep everyone safe, particularly in the event that you lose power during and after the storm.

“If you live by the coast, you should be thinking about storm surge, rainfall, and wind speed,” says Stephen Mullens, a meteorologist and assistant instructional professor of meteorology at the University of Florida’s Department of Geography. “Most fatalities and property damage comes from flooding as a result of both storm surge (water that has been moved from the ocean onto land) and from too much rain during the storm.”
The below preparedness tips are key for dealing with common problems during a hurricane, including flooding, power outages, broken windows from strong winds and fallen trees.

Watch for an evacuation warning: “If you are by the coast, look up whether you are in an evacuation zone,” says Mullens. “If you must evacuate during a storm, you only need to travel just outside the evacuation zone.” State government officials will traditionally issue evacuation warnings at least a few days ahead of a hurricane if not more, depending on what category the storm falls under. Be sure to stay on top of news updates. “You will need to leave before the wind and rain arrives, so your home preparations must happen with a deadline in mind,” says Mullens.

Prepare for flooding: Flooding is not only dangerous and a threat to your safety, but it can also cause irreparable damage to your home, which, even with insurance, can be extremely costly to deal with. Mullens recommends using things like sandbags to blockade your home if possible. “These can help prevent water from seeping under [home] doors and garage doors. Most of the time, you won’t experience the worst-case scenario, and sandbags can really help when flooding is only a few inches,” says Mullens. “No amount of [sandbags] will allow you to stay in an evacuation zone [though]. If flooding is forecast to be more than a foot, then plan to evacuate in case the forecast gets worse or your emergency management deems evacuation to be mandatory.”

Mullens also recommends preparing other areas around your home for excess water, too. “Outside your home, clear your gutters and drainage areas of leaves and other debris,” he says. “You don’t want water backing up and pooling in ways you don’t expect.” If your home does get flooded, there is a very short window of time before it will cause mold growth and become a pain to handle, according to Mullens. “It’s a race against time to prevent the build up of mold in drywall and furniture. If your roof has been damaged, a large tarp will prevent future rain from entering your home,” he says. “Inside, fans and a lot of towels will help dry things out.”

Prepare for strong winds: “To prepare for wind, trim branches on trees and bushes so they won’t hit the house. Bring furniture and outdoor decorations inside,” says Mullens. “For large items, stake and tie them down or they will likely fly away. If you live near the coast, nailing plywood over your windows can prevent damage inside your home from flying debris.” Additionally, make sure your cars aren’t beside trees, especially ones with coconuts or large branches that could fall during the hurricane and damage the body, windows or windshields.

Keep electronics charged: Make sure all your electronics are charged before the storm arrives and be sure to stock up on batteries as needed for things like flashlights and other essential devices. “Charge phones while power remains,” says Mullens. “Write down important information in case your phone’s battery runs out before power is restored.” Depending on the severity of the storm, a power outage is very likely, even if it’s just temporary.

Gas generators are one of the most common appliances that people use to restore power in their homes during and after hurricanes, according to Mullens. If you don’t have or plan on using a generator, there are alternatives you can consider, too. Some batteries work for home appliances, not just small handheld electronic devices, according to Mullens. “Today, large batteries can power an air conditioner, well pump, refrigerator, oven, or microwave for several hours,” says Mullens. “It’s important to assess what you most want to have power during an extended power outage, your ability to store the unit when you don’t need it, and cost to guide your purchases.”

Prepare for a disruption in water supply: A loss in access to clean water is also a common issue during and after a hurricane, so it’s important to make sure you have a plan in case you don’t have water for a few days. “Buy large water jugs for drinking and sanitation. Fill them with water prior to a storm,” says Mullens. “You can also fill a bath tub with water so you can flush your toilets. Most storms won’t be the worst-case scenario, but if it does happen you will want enough water for drinking and food for seven days.”

Buy non-perishable foods: Since losing power is common during and after hurricanes, you won’t have access to traditional kitchen appliances like a refrigerator to keep food fresh, an electric stovetop and oven or microwave, unless you find batteries or power stations suitable for powering them. Be sure to buy shelf-stable foods that don’t require cooking or refrigeration after opening, including canned vegetables and soup, cereal, granola bars, chips and crackers. “All these items can be stored at room temperature for a year unless otherwise noted,” says Mullens. “In the summer, before hurricane season, purchase one to two of these items each shopping trip instead of right before a storm.”

Frequently asked questions

It’s extremely important to not wait until the last minute to buy emergency hurricane supplies, since options will be very limited. Be sure to prepare for the most common problems, like flooding, lack of access to fresh water (including for your toilet), fallen trees and branches and power outages, says Mullens. You can do this by buying things like non-perishable foods, bottled water or gallons of water, medication, power stations and making sure your electronics (including your phone) are fully charged.

Since hurricanes often lead to power outages, you should stock up on things that being without power would affect, Mullens. This includes getting multi-gallon water jugs from stores like Home Depot, Lowe’s or Amazon so you can keep a large supply of water. You should also buy non-perishable foods that don’t have to be refrigerated, including canned foods and dry pantry items. Lastly, you should also stock up on energy by charging all of your portable devices, including a portable power station, and have enough batteries for emergency devices like flashlights.

Yes. While hurricanes are definitely a threat to coastlines, areas far from coasts aren’t exempt from experiencing their effects. Additionally, trailers and mobile homes are particularly vulnerable to damage from hurricanes, according to Mullens.

"Trailers and mobile homes are lighter and more likely to be damaged than homes built on a foundation. Thinner walls mean debris thrown in the wind are more likely to damage walls and windows,” says Mullens. “Being lighter means wind and flood water is more likely to lift the home off its supports. There may be less to do inside and outside to prepare the home itself, but you will likely need to evacuate earlier than recommended.”

While generators are a great appliance when it comes to providing a lot of power during a hurricane, they also can be dangerous when used improperly because they can expose you to carbon monoxide, according to Mullens.

"If you are using a gas-powered generator, the unit must be placed outside with cords running from the generator into the house. It is very common for people to operate generators indoors or in a garage, resulting in the resident dying due to a build-up of carbon monoxide,” he says. “If you are using a large battery, you may want to incorporate solar panels or another method to recharge it in case of an extended outage.”

title: This is the dorm registry I wish I had as a college freshman
summary: A dorm registry can help you pull together everything you need for college — including bedding, supplies and more — and give friends and family an easy way to help.
story: When I moved into my college dorm as a freshman,  I remember wishing there was a simple way to send friends and family a list of everything I still needed — similar to the registries people create for weddings and baby showers. Between bedding, storage, laundry supplies, toiletries and all the little things I didn’t realize I’d need until move-in day, the shopping added up quickly. I wanted a way to make a cohesive list that everyone could shop while avoiding bad communication that resulted in duplicates and deficits.

Since then, I’ve led the back-to-school shopping for my family. I handled my own college shopping and helped my brother, who’s now a senior in college, with his move in. Next up is my sister, who’s a senior in high school, and I’m already thinking about what she’ll need when it’s her turn to move into a dorm. This time, though, I’m making a registry.

A dorm registry can serve two purposes: It keeps your college shopping organized in one place, and it gives friends and family who want to support you an easy way to buy something you’ll actually use. Most if not all retailers keep track of what requests have been fulfilled so there won’t be any duplicate purchases and, depending on the retailer, you may also be able to have items shipped or picked up at a store near your college, which can be particularly helpful if you’re moving far from home or need to fly to school.

As someone who worked for her campus Residential Life office throughout all four years of college and helped support countless move ins and move outs, I know which dorm essentials students actually use (and which ones they probably don’t need). So below, I’ve rounded up places where you can create a dorm registry or shareable wishlist, along with the essentials I’d recommend adding before move-in day.
Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter.
Where can you make a dorm registry?

Not every retailer offers a dedicated dorm registry, but that doesn’t mean you can’t make one. Many stores offer shareable wishlists that accomplish essentially the same thing: You can add the dorm essentials you need, send the list to friends and family and keep everything organized in one place. Below are the retailers I recommend for creating a dorm registry or wishlist, including options that offer shipping or pickup near campus.Note that all these retailers require an account, but the wishlist creation tools are free.
Amazon

Why I like it for college: Amazon is probably one of the easiest options for a dorm registry because you can put a wide variety of dorm essentials (bedding, storage, school supplies, tech accessories, toiletries and more) in one place. You can also assign priorities to items, which I like for distinguishing between the things you need before move-in and the things that would simply be nice to have.

Amazon doesn’t have a registry specifically for dorm rooms, but you can create a Gift List or Wish List and use it like one. To make a Gift List, go to Amazon’s Registry & Gifting page, select “Create” and choose the occasion you’re celebrating; you can also create a List through “Account & Lists” or directly from a product page. Once it’s set up, add dorm essentials as you shop.

How friends and family shop it: You can make an Amazon Gift List public and searchable or keep it shareable and send the link directly to who you want to have it. Amazon also tracks purchases, which helps prevent loved ones from buying the same items.

Shipping/pickup: You can assign a shipping address to an Amazon List, which makes this particularly useful if you want gifts sent to the address you’ll use while at college or mail room once your mailing ID is assigned. Items can be sent directly to your home address which is nice if you want to have safely, securely packaged boxes ready to go for move-in day.
Target

Why I like it for college: Target has nearly everything you might need for a dorm, but its large store footprint is what makes it particularly convenient. If you’re attending college away from home, you can shop before you leave and potentially pick up things closer to school instead of packing every pillow, storage bin and bottle of detergent into the car. Target has almost 2,000 locations across the U.S.

Target is one of my favorite options for this because it actually offers a College Wish List specifically designed for school planning. You can create one on Target.com  or in the Target app, then add products online or by scanning items in a Target store. Target also offers college-focused checklists to help you figure out what you might be missing.

How friends and family shop it: You can send friends and family a direct link — including a customized URL — or make your list searchable on target.com and in Target stores. When someone buys an item directly through the list, Target updates it to help keep track of what’s already been purchased.

Shipping/pickup: This is where I think Target really shines for college students. Gifts can be shipped to the address attached to your list, and shoppers can also purchase registry and wishlist items online for order pickup. Target also offers drive-up pickup and same day delivery, depending on the order and location.
Walmart

Why I like it for college: Walmart is especially useful for the less exciting dorm purchases that are just as important as your bedding and decor — think cleaning products, toiletries, laundry supplies, snacks and class supplies. Its pickup option also makes it useful for replenishing essentials once you’re already on campus.

For dorm shopping, I’d recommend creating a Walmart Wishlist. Walmart says its former “Any Occasion” registries are now wishlists, which can be created on walmart.com or in the Walmart app by going to lists under the “My Items” tab, and then “Create a Wishlist.” You can add products online, through the app or even in store by scanning a product’s barcode.

How friends and family shop it: Once you’ve created your wishlist, you can share it via a copied URL, email or social media. Unlike Walmart’s traditional gift registries, wishlists aren’t searchable by friends and family, so you’ll need to send them the link. Gift givers can purchase products, mark them as purchased and have eligible items shipped directly to you.

Shipping/pickup: Walmart offers both shipping and local pickup/delivery services, although fulfillment options depend on the product and location. For pickup orders, you select a local store and time slot and Walmart notifies you when the order is ready.
Dormify

Why I like it for college: Dormify takes a lot of the guesswork out of college shopping because you aren’t sorting through products intended for an entire house. The site is centered on dorm-friendly categories and features an extensive checklist for students that helps structure shopping plan — including twin XL bedding, storage and organization, bath and laundry, lighting and no-nails decor — so it’s a particularly good option for first-year students furnishing their space for the first time.

Unlike most of the retailers on this list, Dormify is specifically focused on college living and has a dedicated Dorm Wishlist. You can create and manage your wishlist through Dormify’s site and add items from its assortment of twin XL bedding, storage, bath and laundry products, seating, decor, lighting and other dorm essentials.

How friends and family shop it: Dormify has a “Find a Wishlist” tool that lets friends and family search using the student’s name, with optional filters, including state. That means relatives don’t necessarily have to keep track of your individual wishlist link to find it.

Shipping/pickup: Dormify also advertises a Pick Up Near Campus program, which is particularly helpful if you had to drive far or fly to school. Dormify does not have standalone brick-and-mortar stores but you can have items shipped to partner retailers by your school, such as Williams Sonoma, Pottery Barn, or West Elm.
MyRegistry.com

Why I like it for college: College students rarely buy everything from one store. A universal registry lets you make one master dorm list without limiting yourself to a single retailer’s inventory. You can also sync existing registries from other retailers into MyRegistry.

MyRegistry is different from most other options on this list because it isn’t a retailer — it’s a universal registry platform. You create a free account and can then use its browser tool or mobile app to add products to one registry from virtually any online retailer. That means your Target sheets, Amazon desk lamp and highlighters from Walmart don’t need to live on three separate lists.

How friends and family shop it: Instead of sending everyone multiple wishlist links, you share one MyRegistry link. When someone chooses an item, they’re directed to the original retailer to complete the purchase. MyRegistry tracks purchased items on the universal list to help prevent duplicates.

Shipping/pickup: It’s important to note that MyRegistry doesn’t fulfill the order itself. Because shoppers ultimately purchase through the retailer that sells the item, shipping, delivery and pickup options are determined by that retailer.
Pottery Barn Teen

Why I like it for college: PB Teen is particularly useful if you want to make your dorm feel more put together while still shopping for practical necessities. Its dorm assortment covers everything from mattress toppers and twin XL bedding to under-bed storage, laundry supplies, shower caddies and desk accessories, so you can build most of your room from one wishlist. I also like that its site has dedicated dorm-shopping tools, including a dorm checklist and Build Your Bed tool, which can be helpful for first-year students who aren’t sure where to start.

Pottery Barn Teen has a dedicated Dorm Wishlist, making it one of the most college-specific options on this list. You can create a wishlist online and add products from PB Teen’s Dorm Shop, which includes twin XL bedding, storage and organization, bath and laundry essentials, lighting, desk accessories and decor.

How friends and family shop it: Once your Dorm Wishlist is set up, friends and family can search for it on PB Teen’s website using your first and last name, with optional filters for your state, birth month and year. PB Teen also lets you manage your list online and link a wishlist that was originally created in one of its stores.

Shipping/pickup: This is one of the biggest reasons I like PB Teen for college students: The retailer has a Pick Up Near Campus program and lets shoppers filter dorm products based on whether they’re eligible for the service. PB Teen also promotes the option to ship orders to a store, which can help you avoid packing bulky dorm purchases and transporting them from home. Availability varies by product and location, so I’d check what’s eligible near your school before placing an order.
Crate & Barrel

Why I like it for college: I see Crate & Barrel as less of an “everything you need for freshman year” option and more useful for higher-quality items that can follow you beyond the dorm. Think bedding, bath essentials, organizers or kitchenware you’ll eventually use in an apartment. Group gifting is also useful for pricier items.

Crate & Barrel doesn’t have a college-specific registry, but it does allow registries for occasions beyond weddings, including housewarmings — consider dorm room shopping like a mini-housewarming. It is an option for someone furnishing their first space. You can create and edit a registry online or through the Crate & Barrel app and add items digitally or with help from an associate in the store.

How friends and family shop it: Friends and family can search for a registry and purchase directly from it, and Crate & Barrel keeps track of purchased gifts. It also offers group gifting, which lets multiple people contribute toward certain higher-priced registry items.
Shipping/pickup: Eligible registry purchases of $49 or more ship free, according to Crate & Barrel.
The Container Store

Why I like it for college: Storage space is one of the biggest challenges in a dorm room, and organization is where The Container Store really stands out. Its dorm checklist includes under-bed storage, bed risers, desktop organizers, hampers, shower caddies, hanging closet organizers, over-the-door storage and stacking drawers — basically the products that help you make use of every inch of a small room. The retailer even recommends choosing free store pickup at a location near campus in its dorm-shopping materials.

The Container Store doesn’t have a college-specific registry, but you can create a Wish List and use it as a dorm registry. You can name your list — something as simple as “[Your Name]’s College Dorm” works — and add the storage and organization products you want to it. The retailer specifically says its wishlists can be used for occasions like graduations and shared with family and friends.

How friends and family shop it: Once you’ve made your list, The Container Store lets you send it via email to friends and family so they can shop from it. Unlike PB Teen’s Dorm Wishlist, however, this isn’t a full-fledged college registry program; it’s better thought of as a shareable wishlist that you can adapt for dorm shopping.

Shipping/pickup: The Container Store offers free in-store and curbside pickup for online orders. You select the store at checkout, and the retailer sends an email or text when the order is ready. That makes it especially helpful if there’s a Container Store near your college: Instead of filling your car with bulky bins, drawers and organizers, you can order online and pick them up closer to campus. Local delivery is also available in select markets.

How to shop for dorm essentials

Shopping for a dorm is different from shopping for a bedroom at home: You’re working with limited space, may be sharing that space with someone else and will likely have to move everything again at the end of the school year. Before you start adding items to your dorm registry or wishlist, these are the factors you should consider.

Set a budget before you start shopping and prioritize necessities over decor and convenience items. Bedding, bath essentials, laundry supplies and a few storage solutions are worth budgeting for first; you can always buy additional organizers, decorations and accessories after you’ve moved in and know what you actually need.

You also don’t need to buy everything new. If you already own towels, hangers, a desk lamp or other items that work for your dorm, bring them rather than replacing them simply because you’re going to college. A registry can also be a good place for more expensive essentials that friends or family may want to contribute to.

Check your school’s housing website for your residence hall’s floor plan, room dimensions and a list of included furniture before buying larger dorm items. Knowing the size of your bed, what’s already provided and how much floor and closet space you’ll have can prevent you from buying things that won’t fit.

I recommend waiting until move-in to buy some organizers for this reason. It’s much easier to determine whether you need another rolling cart or set of drawers once you unpack and can actually see the space you’re working with.

Read your college’s residence hall policies before buying appliances, furniture or anything that attaches to the walls or doors. Schools can have specific rules about items like microwaves, mini fridges, coffee makers, extension cords, candles and wall-mounted products, and your school may already provide some of the larger items you’re considering.
Don’t forget about your actual dorm room door, either. Check rules and measurements before buying over-the-door organizers, hooks and similar products, since door dimensions and policies can vary.

Coordinate with your roommate before buying anything you only need one of, such as a rug, vacuum, trash can or other shared supplies. Decide who will bring each item rather than splitting the cost of everything, if possible — it’ll make figuring out who takes what at the end of the year much easier.

I’d also avoid relying on your roommate for personal essentials you’ll use frequently. Sharing a vacuum is one thing; having to track down your roommate every time you need laundry pods or utensils is another.

Before buying something, consider how frequently you’ll use it and whether your college already gives you access to one. Many campuses have resources like printers and other school supplies in libraries, computer labs or residence halls, so you may not need your own version of everything.

For inexpensive items you’ll use constantly, having your own may still be worth the convenience. But if something is expensive, bulky and only useful a few times a semester, check what’s available on campus first.

Prioritize durability for products you expect to use throughout college, especially items that will be packed, unpacked and transported repeatedly. Hampers, storage bins, luggage and organizers can take a beating during move-ins and move-outs, so spending a little more on sturdy versions may make sense if you plan to use them for several years.
For inexpensive items you don’t expect to keep after college, durability may matter less. Think about the item’s expected lifespan before deciding where it’s worth spending more.

Think about where everything will go when you move out before buying bulky furniture, storage or decor. If you’re flying home, live far from campus or don’t have much storage space at home, you’ll need to either transport your belongings, pay to store them near school, sell or donate them or replace them the following year.
Collapsible, stackable and multipurpose products can be especially useful for this reason. The less space something takes up when you’re not using it, the easier your end-of-year move will be.

Wait on nonessential storage, decor and convenience products if you’re unsure whether they’ll fit or whether you’ll actually use them. Moving in with the basics and shopping for the rest afterward can save you money and keep you from overcrowding your room.

This is also where ordering for pickup near campus can come in handy. Instead of transporting every possible item from home, you can make a list of things you may need and order eligible products once you’ve seen your room and figured out what’s missing.
Frequently asked questions

A dorm registry is a shareable list of items you need for your college dorm room. It works similarly to a wedding or baby registry, allowing friends and family to see what you need and, depending on the retailer, which items have already been purchased.

Not necessarily, but a shareable wishlist can work essentially the same as a dorm registry. Some retailers offer dedicated college registries or dorm wishlists, while others let you create and share a general wishlist with friends and family.

You can start making a dorm registry once you know where you’ll be living and what your college provides or allows in its residence halls. Starting early also gives you time to compare prices and coordinate larger purchases with your roommate.

Yes, you can make dorm registries or wishlists at multiple retailers. You can share each list separately or use a universal registry service, like MyRegistry.com, to combine products from multiple stores into one list.

You should buy the essentials you’ll need immediately, including bedding, toiletries, towels, laundry supplies and basic organization products. You can wait to buy some storage, decor and other nonessential items until you’ve seen your room and know how much space you actually have.

Don’t add appliances, furniture or other large items until you’ve checked your college’s residence hall rules and what your room already includes. Schools may prohibit certain appliances and often provide items like a desk, chair, dresser or mini fridge.

You might. A dorm registry or wishlist can be useful for returning college students who need to replace or upgrade their essentials. It can also be helpful for someone moving into a different type of housing or whose needs have changed.

title: Missing New York City grandmother found dead near airport in Las Vegas
summary: The body of a missing 63-year-old grandmother from New York City was found near Harry Reid International Airport in Las Vegas, police said Friday.
story: The body of a missing 63-year-old grandmother from New York City was found near Harry Reid International Airport in Las Vegas, police said Friday.
Police said security camera footage showed that Alisa Goods had fallen down an embankment and collapsed and couldn’t be seen from the adjacent roadway, Wayne Newton Boulevard.
Her body was found in a drainage ditch near a parking structure Thursday after someone called to report a body near the airport, the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department said in a statement.
The security video is from Aug. 8, it said, the day Goods’ family said she went missing in Las Vegas while visiting a friend. Goods was from Brooklyn, family has said.
Alana Calloway, Goods’ niece, said her aunt was visiting a friend in Las Vegas and was headed to a pharmacy before she disappeared.
Her family said that after her disappearance, someone using her phone number texted relatives to ask for help in the form of bitcoin or a CashApp transfer.
Family of woman missing in Las Vegas plead for answers
Police believe the texts may have come from scammers using “spoofing” technology to present themselves as texting under Goods’ number. They said they didn’t believe Goods was in danger at the time.
Police said the remains’ identity was preliminary. The cause and manner of death were unavailable.
Calloway said the family is grieving.

“Our hearts are broken,” she said in a statement Friday. “Words cannot describe the pain our family is experiencing right now. We just want to thank the public for the outpouring of love, support, and prayers.”

title: Karoline Leavitt to work for Trump-affiliated super PAC after leaving White House
summary: Press secretary Karoline Leavitt will work for President Donald Trump’s super PAC MAGA Inc.
story: Press secretary Karoline Leavitt will work for President Donald Trump’s super PAC MAGA Inc. after she leaves her post at the White House, she said Friday.

Leavitt, 28, told reporters aboard Air Force One that she will return to work for the super PAC, for which she served as a spokesperson before joining Trump’s 2024 campaign, though she did not specify what her new title will be.
MAGA Inc. did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Leavitt’s new role.

Speaking briefly in the press cabin before takeoff, Leavitt told reporters that she will miss the job “but I love my kids even more.” Leavitt added that she and her family will remain in Washington for a while, telling reporters, “You guys will still see me all the time.”

She told reporters that Friday’s flight to South Carolina for a rally supporting Sen. Darline Graham will be her last trip as press secretary, but that she’ll be back on board for the Republican National Committee’s midterm convention scheduled for Sept. 9 and 10.
Leavitt, who became the youngest press secretary in history when she joined the second Trump administration, announced her departure from the White House on Aug. 12.
Trump wrote in a Truth Social post that day that Leavitt was stepping down to “spend more time with her beautiful young children and family.”

The president added that Leavitt “will now be one of my top outside advisors, and an influential voice within the Republican Party, as we work to defy History, and conclusively win the Midterm Elections.”

Leavitt, who gave birth to her second child in May and returned from maternity leave on July 16, wrote in her own post on Aug. 12 that she “felt in my heart that I cannot be the best mom my two young children deserve while devoting the constant time, energy, and attention required of the White House Press Secretary.”
Leavitt worked as an assistant White House press secretary during Trump’s first term before she became the communications director for Rep. Elise Stefanik, R-N.Y.
Leavitt then ran for Congress in New Hampshire, losing to Democratic Rep. Chris Pappas in 2022. She subsequently began working as a spokesperson for MAGA Inc.

After joining Trump’s 2024 campaign, Leavitt gave birth to her first child and returned to work just four days into her maternity leave in the wake of the assassination attempt against Trump at a rally in Butler, Pennsylvania.

As Leavitt leaves her role after 18 months on the job, she will become the second-longest-serving press secretary under Trump after now-Arkansas Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders, who served in the role for almost two years during Trump’s first term.

title: Supreme Court temporarily allows Trump ballroom construction to continue
summary: Supreme Court rules on whether Trump can move forward with construction on the White House ballroom.
story: WASHINGTON — The Supreme Court on Friday allowed President Donald Trump to continue constructing, at least for now, a new ballroom adjoining the White House.
Chief Justice John Roberts issued a temporary stay that blocks lower court rulings that would have put the aboveground portion of the project on hold.
But the decision is only provisional, giving the justices more time to consider next steps.

The legal challenge has been brought by the National Trust for Historic Preservation, which argued that the president did not have authority to demolish the East Wing of the White House and build a ballroom. One key issue in the case is whether the trust has legal standing to sue based on one of its members objecting on aesthetic grounds.
“To be clear, this is not a final decision on the merits of the government’s stay application, and we await further action,” a trust spokesman said.
Trump praised the court’s decision in a post on TruthSocial.

“We are grateful for the Decision of the United States Supreme Court,” he wrote. “The Military/Ballroom Complex being built on the hallowed grounds of the White House, which is so vital for National Security, will be THE GREATEST OF ITS KIND!”
Trump added that “construction is under budget and ahead of schedule.”

In court filings, the administration has said that as of Aug. 14, construction was 65% complete on the $400 million, privately funded project, with a 250-person crew working 20 hours a day, seven days a week.
The plan includes an extensive underground component, including secure locations and medical facilities that the administration has argued are vital for security.
A federal judge had ruled in favor of the trust, saying that while the underground construction could move forward, the ballroom itself could not be built while litigation continued.
On Aug. 7, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit upheld that decision, setting the deadline of Friday for construction to halt unless the Supreme Court intervened.

title: Trump says loyalist Ed Martin to leave the DOJ to focus on election-related legal battles
summary: Trump loyalist Ed Martin, a “Stop the Steal” organizer and advocate and attorney for Jan. 6 defendants, who later served in the Justice Department, is leaving the administration to focus on upcoming elections.
story: Trump loyalist Ed Martin, a “Stop the Steal” advocate who then served in the Justice Department, is leaving the administration to focus on upcoming elections, the president announced Friday.

“Ed Martin has been with me from the very beginning, and done an incredible job as an Attorney, Director of the Weaponization Working Group, and the United States Attorney for the District of Columbia,” Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social.

“Ed is now leaving to go outside to fight Legal Battles for the upcoming Midterm Election, and the Presidential Election of 2028. I know he will do an outstanding job, ensure Free, Fair, and Honest Elections, and strongly advance our Constitutional Rights. Good luck Ed!”
Attorney General Todd Blanche praised Martin in a post on X, calling him “a patriot who loves this nation.” “We look forward to seeing his future successes!” Blanche wrote.
Martin’s most recent role in the administration was as pardon attorney at the Justice Department.

Despite his lack of prosecutorial experience, Trump appointed Martin to serve as the interim U.S. attorney for Washington, D.C., beginning in January 2025. There he oversaw the firings of Jan. 6 prosecutors, demoted others and opened an investigation into the office’s handling of the Capitol riot investigation.
Trump later withdrew Martin’s formal nomination for the permanent position amid a difficult Senate confirmation process.

“If Mr. Martin were being put forth as a U.S. attorney for any district except the district where Jan. 6 happened, the protest happened, I’d probably support him, but not in this district,” Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., a key member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, said at the time.

Trump then announced Martin would be appointed associate deputy attorney general and pardon attorney, and that he would direct a “weaponization working group” at the Justice Department. That group was tasked with investigating prosecutors who pursued past investigations into the president and his allies.
In February 2026, NBC News reported he was stripped of his role leading the weaponization working group.
On Friday, Martin reposted Trump’s announcement of his government departure, adding, “Proud to serve. Fight Fight Fight.”

title: Love Jimothy? Meet Meemers, The Adorable Cat With Short Spine Syndrome
summary: For fans of the perfectly imperfect Jimothy the Raccoon, there’s now another furry friend over which we can all obsess.
story: For fans of the perfectly imperfect Jimothy the Raccoon, there’s now another furry friend over which we can all obsess.

Readers, meet Meemers: The adorable rescue cat who has short-spine syndrome, the same condition that Jimothy is also believed to have. The two-and-a-half-year-old feline, who’s based in Bloomington, Illinois, recently went viral for her barely-there neck and resemblance to Seattle’s beloved raccoon. One video of Meemers, posted Aug. 18, has drawn more than 41 million views as of Aug. 22.

Owner Katie Dahlen, who previously worked at the shelter where Meemers was found, has always loved making clips for social media. But, Dahlen tells TODAY.com, that she never expected the video of Meemers to go viral seemingly overnight.

“I missed making videos, and I was like, ‘Well, I have this awesome cat, and I want to share her with people,’” Dahlen says. “I just didn’t realize how big she would blow up in a 24-hour span. It was crazy.”
In the video, Meemers, in her black, fluffy glory, simply sits down. There’s a few shots of Meemers giving her best Blue Steel as well. And it’s truly easy to see why she’s so beloved.
“Sensational whiskers / body tea / no notes 🖤” one fan replied.
Another demanded a collab between Meemers, Jimothy and Tilly, the famous pup who also has short spine syndrome.

Meemers is certainly unique. From her shoulders to the base of her tail, she’s only about seven-and-a-half inches long. She also has a slight tail deformity. For Dahlen, who’s had Meemers for over a year now, it was love at first sight.

“She was actually left at the shelter in a box outside,” Dahlen says of the shelter at which she was working at the time. “Literally, from the day she came in, I was like, ‘She needs to come home with me.’”
Meemers was, at first, not in the greatest shape, Dahlen says. The fur around her butt was matted and there was an abscess in the area as well, Dahlen explains.

“The owner had tried to shave her, so you could tell they cared, but maybe they didn’t have the resources, and they were embarrassed about walking her in through the doors,” Dahlen says. “So they left her out front.”
After Meemers was given a course of antibiotics and some TLC, she was ready to head home with Dahlen. And since July 2025, Dahlen said she and her husband have been enjoying their adorable cat.

Given her deformities, Meemers has had to make a couple of adjustments in order to thrive, Dahlen says. She doesn’t climb much and she’s unable to jump. Because her organs are squished in her very small body, she needs to be held a certain way, Dahlen says. The feline also overheats quite easily.

“I always equate her to being kind of like a pug, where she overheats easily if it’s too warm outside,” she says. Dahlen adds that if Meemers over-exerts herself, she’ll start panting. “So a lot of her supervised outside time in her backyard is in the evening when it’s cooler.”
Dahlen points out that Meemers has “virtually no neck,” so she’s unable to successfully groom her own back. That’s where Dahlen comes in.

“I brush her multiple times a day. If I’m sitting down, watching TV in the evening, she’s sitting on my lap and I’m grooming her,” Dahlen says. “She gets the occasional bath because I can only redistribute the oils in her coat so much with brushing.”
Though none of that has stopped Meemers from having an infectious personality. She’s a people person, er, cat, Dahlen says. And she’s quite social.
“She loves people,” Dahlen says. “I can literally take her out like anywhere on leash.”
Meemers also loves being pet, and often returns the favor with chatty little meows that Dahlen likens to the sound that Spongebob’s pet Gary the snail makes.
“She loves to be held, but you have to hold her right,” Dahlen says. “When you pet her, she will talk.”
As for Meemers’ incredible name? Well, Dahlen says it’s actually a moniker that evolved from the cat’s original name Mila.

“I was calling her ‘Mimi.’ I was calling her ‘Mealy Bug,’ and then ‘Meemers’ just kind of came up,” Dahlen says of the cat’s now one true government name. “Then she was really only responding to that.”
Dahlen says she’s been pleased with the positive reception to her Meemers and hopes that fans can learn from the sweet cat.
“Give special needs cats a chance,” Dahlen says. “They definitely do require a little adaptation at home, but they are so worth it.”

title: Man Who’s Rated Over 300 Benches Gives Out Only Perfect Score For The Sweetest Reason
summary: Sam Wilmot, who runs @ratethisbench on Instagram, finally gave out an elusive perfect score to the bench at which he got married.
story: Bench your plans, take a seat and listen to a tale that’s sweet as can be from top-to-bottom.

Sam Wilmot, a 29-year-old based in Bristol, England, has rated more than 300 benches through his Instagram page @ratethisbench, he tells TODAY.com. With a strict criteria in place, Wilmot has never given out a perfect 10 — that is, until he recently revisited one particular bench with his beau, Sophie, on their wedding day.

The post about the bench — one that sits outside of the striking 13th century church St. John the Baptist in the village of Old Sodbury — has since gone viral as shocked fans have long been waiting for that elusive 10/10. Wilmot, who’s not in it for fame, says that for him, the bench will forever be associated with the “best day of my life,” Wilmot tells TODAY.com.

“I’d always held back a mark for the “wow” factor, and previously scored this bench a 9/10. But the overwhelming feeling of joy and awe in this moment is the wow,” Wilmot wrote in the caption of the photo, posted in June. “No moment or bench will ever come close to this for me, I can proudly say I have found my 10. In Sophie, and this bench. Sophie Alicia Wilmot, I love you.”

Wilmot has rated everything from a department store bench that featured Paddington Bear, which scored a 6/10, to a carved, wooden bench outside of England’s National Coal Mining Museum, which was given a 5/10. And each post comes with a description and some interesting facts and reflections in addition to the score rationale.

To make things fair, Wilmot scores everything on a rubric, he says. There’s up to three marks for location and view, one mark for having a concrete or solid base for accessibility in all seasons, another mark for being made out of wood and a mark for having a plaque or dedication, he says.
Wilmot also considers functionality. There’s a mark for having an armrest or back support along with another one for curvature of the seat, an important aspect of comfortability, he says.
“Then, really, the tenth mark is a ‘wow factor,’” Wilmot says. “Something that makes it stand out significantly, or is inspiring.”
